3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: Morning haze surrounded the city of Deyr as the sun dawned on the Day of Descension. The holiest day of the Nurity religion, it celebrated the first message received from God by Saint Dast and his thirty disciples.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: As per tradition, the celebration was held inside the Archsanctuary of Dastnurity, closed to the public eye.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: That was Lucian's idea. As he saw it, granting the people a rare glimpse of the Grand Ceremony, and showing them how seriously their President took this holy event, would ease any tensions that lingered in the region.

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: And so we arrived at the largest cathedral in Sordland. A huge crowd gathered around our convoy as our car pulled up to the entrance.

7.speaker: Lucian Galade
7.text: “This will work out well. Trust me, sir.”

8.speaker: Lucian Galade
8.text: “Of course, that's only if the prayer is done completely correctly. Please don't forget the order.”

9.speaker: Lucian Galade
9.text: “First, you will need to grasp the holy sceptre with your left hand, then touch the altar with your right. Kneel before the Archpriest and wait for him to put the sword on your shoulder.”

13.speaker: Player
13.text: “I didn't understand a word you just said.”

14.speaker: Lucian Galade
14.text: “Just do your best to remember it. We can't afford to lose our religious base over this."

16.speaker: Lucian Galade
16.text: “It's 'just' one of the most important ceremonies in Sordland. Especially for Deyr's Bludish residents.”

17.speaker: Lucian Galade
17.text: “You will have to go first. I will come inside later and we will meet up after your part is done. Good luck, sir.”

19.speaker: Narrator
19.text: The Archsanctuary was a sight to see. With its towering visage, it cast a shadow over a large portion of the city. I had to crane my neck to see the narrow spires at the top. Just standing next to it made me feel awe and dread in equal measure.

20.speaker: Narrator
20.text: As I reached the gates, I spotted my welcoming committee. The Archpriest and his disciples were waiting for my arrival. At my approach, they all bowed their heads in respect.

21.speaker: Archpriest
21.text: “Mr. President. Praise God! It is a blessing to see you on our most holy day again. Welcome, welcome.”

22.speaker: Narrator
22.text: He led me through the main hall, which had a stratospheric ceiling and Nurist icons lining the walls. We walked up a creaking spiral staircase to the top floor and finally arrived in front of the confession chamber.

23.speaker: Player
23.text: “Thank you. It is nice to be here in Deyr again.”

25.speaker: Player_Italic
25.text: Bow your head before the Archpriest.

26.speaker: Archpriest
26.text: “Shall we move inside for your confession?”

28.speaker: Player_Italic
28.text: Pull the Archpriest aside for a photo.

30.speaker: Narrator
30.text: The Archpriest gave me an infectious smile as he straightened back up. Tall and handsome, in his mid-50s, he was one of the youngest and most popular Archpriests in history. Some of his more avid followers even likened him to Saint Dast.

31.speaker: Archpriest
31.text: “Oh, great people of Sordland! Once again we are gathered here to honor the Day of Descension!”

32.speaker: Narrator
32.text: The crowd was still cheering loudly. The Archpriest turned and raised both of his hands, and everyone immediately fell silent.

33.speaker: Archpriest
33.text: “I am indescribably happy to be sharing this moment with you as well as every Blud and Sord, old and young, tuning in to their television to watch this holy commemoration!”

34.speaker: Archpriest
34.text: “Along with the leader of our great nation, I say: Let the holy day begin!”

35.speaker: Narrator
35.text: He smiled beatifically as the crowd burst into rapturous applause. After it subsided, he turned to me.

36.speaker: Narrator
36.text: We made our way downstairs where the ceremony was already in progress. The choir sang angelically as the Archpriest took his position beside the altar. When they finished their hymn, an expectant silence fell over the room. It was time for my part.

37.speaker: Narrator
37.text: I started my walk, bowed and approached the altar.

38.speaker: Player_Italic

39.speaker: Player_Italic

44.speaker: Player_Italic

185.text: He led me through the thousand-year-old corridors to his office. The smell of dust and old tomes was in the air, along with the scent of burning incense being prepared for the ceremony.

187.speaker: Narrator
187.text: The wooden chair next to him looked like it might turn to dust at a single touch. I sat down gingerly. It was surprisingly sturdy.

192.speaker: Archpriest
192.text: “Happens to the best of us. It will be televised, after all.”

198.speaker: Archpriest
198.text: “I wanted to talk to you about something.”

199.speaker: Narrator
199.text: He leaned back in his chair comfortably.

203.speaker: Archpriest
203.text: “I wanted to talk to you about something.”

204.speaker: Archpriest
204.text: “I realize it has been months since the Benfi Festival, but this is my first chance to bring it up with you. It's about the actions of the First Lady."

205.speaker: Archpriest
205.text: “I wanted to give you something. A gift to celebrate this special day.”

206.speaker: Archpriest
206.text: “As you know, the festival is a holy event. Letting a woman make the opening speech did not sit well with us. We share the same concerns as Mr. Leste."

207.speaker: Archpriest
207.text: “A woman's place is beside her family, not giving public speeches in revealing dresses. Certainly not insulting the important traditions behind such an event.”

208.speaker: Archpriest
208.text: “Of course we cannot ask you to do anything about it. She is your wife. But I just wanted to voice our disproval of the situation. A woman presiding over such an important religious event. What have we become?”

210.speaker: Narrator
210.text: Disgust was apparent on his face.

211.speaker: Player
211.text: “I agree. It was my fault. Won't happen again.”

212.speaker: Player
212.text: “I let her do the speech because people like you still exist in Sordland.”

213.speaker: Archpriest
213.text: “Wonderful. Thank you for listening to our concerns, Mr. President.”

214.speaker: Archpriest
214.text: “You are right, Mr. President. I just wanted to voice our opinion on the matter.”

215.speaker: Narrator
215.text: His face soured and he did not reply. He looked me up and down for a moment.

219.speaker: Archpriest
219.text: “I also heard you decided on the new curriculum...”

220.speaker: Archpriest
220.text: “...And decided that creationism shall no longer be taught in Sordland's schools. Needless to say, both I and the Sanctuary are outraged."

221.speaker: Archpriest
221.text: “The possibility that entire generations of schoolchildren will have their minds filled with nonsense about 'evolution' while failing to learn one of the main tenets of Nurity... it will hurt us for years to come."

222.text: “Religion doesn't belong in schools. Just like it doesn't belong in my government's policies.”

223.speaker: Player
223.text: “I didn't want to ban creationism. There were extenuating circumstances."

224.text: “I did not ask you for your opinion.”

225.speaker: Archpriest
225.text: “What kind of circumstances allow such a--.”

229.speaker: Archpriest

232.text: He opened the box and showed me what was inside.

233.speaker: Narrator
233.text: It was a dagger. The handle looked like it was made of pure gold and had a very large gem at the end. On the blade, the words were inscribed: "Vectern sis da!". Victory is close. On the other side, another set of words: "King Egmund".

234.speaker: Archpriest
234.text: “This dagger belonged to King Egmund. It is a very important artifact of the Kingdom of Sordland era. It is now yours, Mr. President.”

237.speaker: Archpriest
237.text: “Yes you can, sir. It is now yours. Think of the past and think of who we are. Traditions are what brought us to this point.”

238.speaker: Archpriest
238.text: “Think of the past and think of who we are. Traditions are what brought us to this point.”

239.speaker: Archpriest
239.text: “Now then, it should be right about time.”

250.speaker: Player
250.text: “I couldn't control myself and hit my wife.”

251.speaker: Archpriest
251.text: “Physical abuse is a sin. But every man can lose his temper. A husband must always support and protect his wife. You have taken the vows and you must uphold them. Repent, and God may forgive you.”

261.speaker: Narrator
261.text: Before we went in, the Archpriest looked at the crowd and pointed at one man. I turned and followed his finger with my eyes.

265.speaker: Narrator
265.text: It was a man holding a picket sign that said: 'Stop The Religious Disharmony Bill'.

266.speaker: Archpriest
266.text: “As you can see, every man has his faults.”

268.speaker: Player
268.text: “I take it you don't approve of the Religious Harmony bill.”

271.speaker: Archpriest
271.text: “Yes, that's right. But today is not the day to discuss that.”

272.speaker: Archpriest
272.text: “But of course. I am but a simple man and a mere servant of God.”
